messages:
jess_mc: Hey team — planning to spend ~10 weeks in Austin starting May 18. Do I need to change my homebase or will this be treated as a temporary remote travel? Also: how does the monthly WFH stipend get handled (prorated?), and any payroll/tax stuff I should be worried about?

olivia_peopleops: @jess_mc thanks for flagging! Short answers: if it's under 90 days it's usually temporary travel (no homebase change), stipend prorates for partial months, and payroll withholding typically stays based on your current homebase unless state tax nexus rules require otherwise. Need some details so we can confirm.

jess_mc: awesome. Exact dates 2026-05-18 to 2026-07-27. Will keep CA as homebase while I go. Also bringing partner + cat — any relocation or pet reimbursement? :)

trevor_finance: For stipend/proration we apply: monthly_stipend_amount * (days_remote_in_month / days_in_month) and round to cents. Send the dates and whether you'll be on company wifi or coworking. For payroll: if you keep CA homebase, we don't change state withholding for under-90-day travel. If you start working in TX >90 days or change homebase, we process a homebase update and update state tax withholding.

sara_legal: Adding legal note: TX has no state income tax, but working there temporarily could create local employer obligations in rare cases if travel is repetitive or tied to clients in-state. File the travel notification form so we can track days — that helps with nexus reporting.

jess_mc: Got it. Where's the travel notification form?

olivia_peopleops: Link in the handbook: https://redwood-internal.company/travel-notify (or go to People Ops > Travel & Location > Temporary Remote). Fill it out ASAP so we can mark your dates. We'll then trigger payroll and benefits checks.

jess_mc: Will do now. Quick question on benefits: do I lose CA healthcare or dental eligibility for those 10 weeks?

sara_legal: Short answer: no, benefits coverage continues while you're an active employee and on approved temporary travel. If you switch homebase permanently we re-evaluate benefits eligibility and carrier rules might require changes.

trevor_finance: One more operational note: if you want the full-month stipend for May, submit the travel form and we'll see whether your remote days fall mostly in June — we prorate May and July. Example: May 18-31 = 14/31 days so stipend = monthly_amount * 14/31.

jess_mc: Perfect. Do I need to do anything for reimbursements for coworking or moving partner's things?

olivia_peopleops: We don't cover personal relocation for short trips. Coworking can be reimbursed if pre-approved under the temporary remote coworking policy — attach receipts and request approval before booking. Partner/pet moves are personal and not covered except in formal relocation packages (which are for permanent moves and require manager + People Ops sign-off).

jess_mc: Understood. Last one: will this impact my payroll bonus/proration or equity vesting dates?
	revor_finance: No impact to vesting or annual bonus plan for approved temporary travel. Payroll pay date and gross compensation remain the same. If you change homebase permanently we do some admin cutovers that could affect benefits effective dates, but vesting is unaffected.

hrbot: Reminder: travel notifications older than 7 days without form submission will generate a follow-up. Please complete the form to avoid extra verifications. :memo:

jess_mc: Thanks all — submitted the form and marked dates. Appreciate the quick help. :heart:
